summary.text: A 33-year-old primigravida (G1P0) at 34 weeks of gestation presented with persistent right upper quadrant pain and epigastric discomfort unrelated to dietary intake. Hepatitis B was found at her initial admission without routine treatment, and she reported no history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, heart disease, surgical procedures, trauma or other medical conditions. Examination noted a large mass in the right upper quadrant.

Laboratory tests showed anemia with hemoglobin 97 g/L, elevated AFP 139.67 ng/mL and PIVKA-II 4926.39 mAU/mL, positive HBsAg, HBeAg and HBcAb, and no quantitative HBV DNA testing. Ultrasound showed a 15.0 × 14.8 cm liver mass, MRI a right liver lesion with normal fetal MRI, and CT a 20 × 18 cm tumor from the right liver lobe. The possibility of HCC was considered, and the disease was classified as AJCC Stage III.

After multidisciplinary discussion and informed consent, anesthesia in the subarachnoid space was used and a healthy newborn was delivered, with a cesarean section at 34 weeks of gestation. A right hepatectomy followed 15 days later under general anesthesia. The resected tumor measured about 225 mm, and histology confirmed well-differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma with CK-L and CD34 staining. Postoperatively she received Sintilimab and Lenvatinib 8 mg/day; a clinical psychology team supported her throughout the perioperative period.

Postoperative recovery was smooth and she was discharged without significant complications. The psychological interventions reduced anxiety scores and improved treatment compliance. Sonazoid-enhanced ultrasound 2 months after surgery showed no recurrence or metastasis, follow-up assessments showed a stable condition, and approximately 2 years post-surgery she remained alive and in good health.
